text:
Maria: Quick sync — ran the co-residency load test (2x small-llama + 1x longctx) on a 48GB GPU and saw a spike of OOMs around step 1400, looks like workspace + KV-cache thrash.
Kai: Can you attach the flame/prof output or the allocator logs?
Maria: Pasting minimal excerpt from allocator log: 
```
[alloc] t=1402 peak=43.7GB slab_hits=84% pool_reclaims=112 reclaim_latency_ms=9
[kvcache] ops=21k hit=72% miss=28% swap_out=3.1GB swap_in=3.4GB
[kernel] selected=trt_fused_fp16 fallback=aten_fp32
```
Maria: Note kernel switch at the same time — fallback to aten_fp32 increases workspace per-layer by ~1.8x.
Devin: Huh. So it's both kernel selection and KV churn. Do we have batching heuristics that cause longer sequences to coalesce into same launch?
Sophie: The batcher groups by model_id but not by sequence length bucket right now. That means a long request can pull a whole micro-batch into large workspace mode.
Kai: Proposed quick mitigation: 1) isolate a tiny reserved pool for long-ctx models, 2) add sequence-length bucketing to the batcher, 3) aggressive buffer reuse between kernel variants.
Maria: I ran a micro-sim where we pre-allocate "mini-pools" per model class (small/medium/long) and backfill from a shared eviction pool. Results: fewer transient OOMs but slightly higher steady-state fragmentation.
Devin: Any numbers?
Maria: From the sim:
```
config A (no buckets): oom_rate=0.23, avg_alloc=41.9GB, reclaim_ops=120
config B (mini-pools + buckets): oom_rate=0.03, avg_alloc=42.6GB, reclaim_ops=68
config C (mini-pools + aggressive reuse): oom_rate=0.01, avg_alloc=43.1GB, reclaim_ops=30
```
Sophie: So aggressive reuse trades slightly higher average allocation for much fewer reclaim ops and OOMs. That seems acceptable for production.
Kai: Reuse needs careful safety checks across kernels — different kernels have different alignment/stride requirements. We can't blindly reuse a buffer sized for aten_fp32 with a trt_fused_fp16 kernel unless we track metadata.
Maria: Agreed. My prototype carries a small header per buffer: {owner_kernel_tags, alignment, max_active_seq_len}. Reuse only if owner_kernel_tags compatible. Cheap check.
Devin: What about KV cache behavior? If we evict KV pages aggressively to shared SSD, we must avoid thrashing when long-ctx requests come back-to-back.
Maria: In the sim I added a hot-resident KV slice for recent prefixes (LRU window) and allow an async prefetch path when we detect canary tokens. That reduced swap_in latency by ~60ms on avg.
Sophie: Nice. For rollout plan: canary 1) batcher length-buckets only, 2) mini-pools with shared eviction, 3) reuse metadata enforcement, 4) KV hot-slice + async prefetch. Roll forward only if latency tail stays within SLO.
Kai: Also add a metric: kernel_switch_count per minute and workspace_variance. If kernel_switch spikes, trigger a revert.
Maria: I will open a small RFC with the sim code & config and include the logs + alloc profiler. Want code owners to review before I wire it into the runtime.
Devin: Tag me when RFC is up, I can help vet the kernel compatibility table.
Sophie: I'll add a dashboard with new metrics (oom_rate, reclaim_ops, kernel_switch_count, kv_swap_io) for the canary.
infra-bot: Scheduled canary deployment for rt/mini-pools-sim at 2026-03-19T14:00Z (ID: canary-rt-1127).
Maria: Thanks — will push RFC shortly. Short-term action: turn on sequence-length bucketing for the hosted test fleet and monitor for 24h.
Kai: Sounds good. If we see regressions, revert and collect traces for a deeper kernel selection replay.
Maria: FYI logs saved to /mnt/prof/1812468102/ — sharing the link in #eng-runtime after RFC.
Sophie: small note — ensure encryption of KV swap files for Private deployments.
Maria: noted.
Maria: (last) thanks all, will follow up with RFC + perf artifacts.
